title: Exploration of purine metabolism-related genes in the development of osteoporosis by integrated analyses and experiments.
authors: Zeng, Yuqing; Hu, Jintao; Lu, Jianwei; Zhu, Yunyun
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过整合分析和实验探索骨质疏松中嘌呤代谢相关基因，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Metabolomics analyses suggest abnormal purine metabolism during the development of osteoporosis. This study aimed to investigate the role of purine metabolism-related genes in osteoporosis. METHODS: Three microarray datasets for osteoporosis were used in this study. Purine metabolism activity score was quantified by GSVA. Differential expression analysis and weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) were employed to screen dysregulated purine metabolism activity-related genes in osteoporosis. Three machine learning algorithms were employed to screen potential biomarkers, and a predictive nomogram based on biomarkers was then established. Drugs that target the biomarkers were predicted based on the DGIDB database. An ovariectomized rat model causing osteoporosis was established to validate the expression of biomarkers and the purine metabolism in vivo. RESULTS: Purine metabolism activity of osteoporosis samples was significantly different from controls. Based on differential analysis and WGCNA, 122 dysregulated purine metabolism-related genes were found, and they were mainly involved in immune inflammation-related functions. PDPK1 and FOXO3 were identified as potential biomarkers, and the nomogram based on PDPK1 and FOXO3 showed well performance to predict the onset risk of osteoporosis, with a clinical net benefit greater than PDPK1 and FOXO3 each alone. Two approved drugs, resveratrol and celecoxib, were predicted to target FOXO3 and PDPK1, respectively. Expression of FOXO3 and PDPK1 was enhanced in osteoporosis both in bioinformatics analysis and in vivo experiments. Rat model showed higher serum levels of xanthine and hypoxanthine as well as high level of uric acid. CONCLUSION: FOXO3 and PDPK1 might be biomarkers and targets for the prevention and treatment of osteoporosis.
abstract_zh: 目的：代谢组学分析提示骨质疏松症发展过程中存在嘌呤代谢异常。本研究旨在探讨嘌呤代谢相关基因在骨质疏松症中的作用。方法：本研究使用了三个骨质疏松症微阵列数据集。通过GSVA量化嘌呤代谢活性评分。采用差异表达分析和加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）筛选骨质疏松症中与嘌呤代谢活性失调相关的基因。运用三种机器学习算法筛选潜在生物标志物，并基于这些标志物建立预测列线图。根据DGIDB数据库预测靶向这些生物标志物的药物。建立去卵巢大鼠骨质疏松模型，以验证生物标志物的表达及体内嘌呤代谢情况。结果：骨质疏松症样本的嘌呤代谢活性与对照组有显著差异。基于差异分析和WGCNA，发现122个失调的嘌呤代谢相关基因，这些基因主要涉及免疫炎症相关功能。PDPK1和FOXO3被确定为潜在生物标志物，基于PDPK1和FOXO3的列线图在预测骨质疏松症发病风险方面表现出良好性能，其临床净收益大于单独使用PDPK1或FOXO3。预测两种已批准药物——白藜芦醇和塞来昔布——分别靶向FOXO3和PDPK1。在生物信息学分析和体内实验中，骨质疏松症中FOXO3和PDPK1的表达均增强。大鼠模型显示血清黄嘌呤和次黄嘌呤水平升高，同时尿酸水平也较高。结论：FOXO3和PDPK1可能是骨质疏松症预防和治疗的生物标志物及靶点。
